profile.behavior: Lower Florida Keys acoustic telemetry documents Permit using both shallow nearshore flats (less than 3 m) and deeper Florida Reef Tract habitat (approximately 15–40 m). The study reported that many tagged fish used both habitat types, supporting a connected flats-and-reef framing rather than a flats-only profile.
profile.life_history: This pilot separates flats-foraging context from deeper reef occupancy and spawning context. The available telemetry evidence does not justify treating every hard-bottom map polygon as spawning habitat.
profile.spawning: The lower Florida Keys telemetry study reported reef occupancy peaking from March through September, especially April–May, and interpreted reef use as associated with spawning. Treat this as study-region evidence, not a fully validated South Florida-wide seasonal rule.
profile.overwintering: No South Florida overwintering route or seasonal refuge rule is encoded in this pilot profile.

factors.value_notes: The configured temperature bounds are legacy screening values, not a validated adult Permit preference or physiological tolerance range. The cited flats-to-reef telemetry study supports habitat use and seasonal reef occupancy, not these numeric SST thresholds. Preserve them only for compatibility until a suitable temperature study and independent local validation are available.
factors.reason_template: Water is {value} C, within the currently configured provisional screening band for Permit; this is not a validated thermal preference.

open_items: Find a primary study supporting adult Trachinotus falcatus thermal tolerance or preferred temperature; do not infer SST thresholds from habitat-use telemetry.
Add a distinct South Florida reef-tract validation sample set representing the documented deeper habitat range; retain flats as a separate habitat role.
Verify bathymetry source resolution, vertical datum, spatial coverage, and freshness before classifying reef-tract depth.
Validate March–September reef occupancy and April–May peak timing against independent observations outside the original telemetry sample.
Separate flats-foraging, reef occupancy/spawning context, seasonal presence, and flats-to-reef connectivity in candidate model dimensions.
Do not treat generic hard-bottom or artificial-reef map classes as confirmed Permit spawning habitat.
Keep current SST range, weight, active state, gate, and required flag unchanged until evidence and validation justify a model change.

timing.note: Angler-derived timing hypotheses only. The numeric light, tide, and front maps are legacy uncalibrated settings, not demonstrated Permit feeding probabilities. Calibrate against timestamped, effort-aware observations before using them as biological claims.

text.falling: Outgoing tide flushes food for Permit.
text.rising: Incoming tide brings bait for Permit.

contexts.notes: Lower Florida Keys telemetry documents use of nearshore flats shallower than 3 m. Validate transfer to individual South Florida flats.
The study documents use of Florida Reef Tract habitat at approximately 15–40 m and seasonal reef occupancy. This does not make every hard-bottom polygon confirmed spawning habitat.
Tagged fish used both nearshore flats and deeper reef habitat. Connectivity is an ecological context, not a route prediction.
